sketches.title: Doom by Dash
sketches.premise: A prophecy is being delivered one line at a time, and the host is already yelling about the ending. Add exactly one new line that follows from every line before it, turning an ordinary event into a bigger, stranger fate. The host praises clever trouble and lovingly mocks anyone who plays it safe.
sketches.criterion: A line HOLDS if it advances the same prophecy by one clear step; a skipped link is a sudden result with no cause, an ending is a final fate that leaves no next step, and an undo is a line that cancels or rewrites what already happened.
sketches.move_shape: Add one prophecy line, not a correction or a second event. Example: "The school fair runs out of lemonade, so the thirsty mayor declares the ducks in charge."
sketches.first_card: The toaster pops up one slice of bread.

sketches.title: Omen Chain
sketches.premise: The first line is a small omen, and each player must make the next omen point more strongly toward one shared fate. Keep building the chain until the future feels impossible to avoid; the host calls every weak link a tiny betrayal of destiny.
sketches.criterion: A line HOLDS if it adds one new sign that makes the same looming fate more likely; a skipped link jumps from clue to conclusion, an ending names the fate instead of adding a sign, and an undo makes an earlier omen meaningless.
sketches.move_shape: Add one omen that connects to all earlier omens. Example: "A crow drops a blue button on the path, and the button matches the king's coat."
sketches.first_card: A single shoe is found in the school hallway.

sketches.title: Future Receipt
sketches.premise: You are writing a receipt from the future, one item at a time, for a purchase that has not happened yet. Each line must explain the next charge or note while making the final purchase more ridiculous; the host cheers costly details and roasts bargain-bin imagination.
sketches.criterion: A line HOLDS if it adds exactly one plausible receipt entry that fits the buyer, purpose, and earlier entries; a skipped link adds a charge without a reason, an ending totals or closes the receipt, and an undo removes or reverses a paid entry.
sketches.move_shape: Add one item, fee, or note to the same future receipt. Example: "One silver umbrella, for rain that falls upward — 8 coins."
sketches.first_card: One paper bag, for carrying something too shy to be seen — 2 coins.

sketches.title: Quest in the Margins
sketches.premise: A prophecy appears in the margins of an ordinary page, one line at a time, and each line sends the hero one step closer to a strange task. Keep the same quest moving forward; the host supplies loud fanfare for useful danger and a gentle slap for random nonsense.
sketches.criterion: A line HOLDS if it adds one doable quest step caused by the current situation; a skipped link jumps past needed action, an ending completes or rewards the quest, and an undo makes the hero abandon or negate a completed step.
sketches.move_shape: Add one next action or discovery in the quest. Example: "To open the locked shed, the hero must trade the mayor's missing hat for a brass key."
sketches.first_card: At sunrise, a map appears under the hero's breakfast plate.

sketches.title: Crown of Consequences
sketches.premise: A prophecy starts with a tiny choice, and every new line shows the next consequence until someone is crowned by the mess they made. Add one consequence at a time, fitting the whole trail; the host worships clever payback and teases anyone who escapes too easily.
sketches.criterion: A line HOLDS if it is one new, believable consequence of the exact choices and events already shown; a skipped link leaps over a needed result, an ending crowns or settles the outcome, and an undo cancels an earlier choice or consequence.
sketches.move_shape: Add one consequence that follows from the current chain. Example: "Because Lina fed the royal cat, it follows her home and exposes the hidden tunnel."
sketches.first_card: A child presses the big red button marked DO NOT PRESS.

sketches.title: Last-Line Lottery
sketches.premise: Each prophecy line narrows the possible ending without saying it outright, like a wild lottery where fate keeps removing choices. Add one new fact that makes some endings impossible and others more likely; the host celebrates sharp clues and mocks anyone who leaves destiny with no homework.
sketches.criterion: A line HOLDS if it adds one new restriction or clue that still allows at least two possible endings; a skipped link removes possibilities without a supporting fact, an ending leaves only one ending, and an undo restores a possibility already ruled out.
sketches.move_shape: Add one clue or rule that narrows the future while keeping more than one ending alive. Example: "The winner must be someone who has never worn a crown, but the prize is still hidden."
sketches.first_card: Tomorrow, someone in the town will receive a mysterious key.
